full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the tenant is directed against the judgment and order of the learned District Judge affirming those of the learned Munsif in a proceeding under section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance; 1963. 

 2. The tenant filed an application before the learned Munsif, 1st Court, Sylhet acting as the Controlling, under Section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, contending inter alia, that he is a monthly tenant under the opposite party landlord in respect of the concerned premises at a rental of Tk. 30/-according to Bengali Calendar month. He paid rent upto Agrahayan, 1373 B. S. and obtained proper rent receipts. According to the tenant, rent for Poush and Magh, 1373 B. S. was paid but the opposite party landlord did not grant any receipt on this or that plea. He thereafter tendered rent for the month of Falgoon and the landlord refused to accept the same. On 16.3.67 he remitted rent for the month of Falgoon by Festal money order which the landlord refused. Thereafter the tenant made the instant application to deposit the rent for the month of Falgoon and the subsequent period. 

 3. The landlord opposite party contested the case traversing the material allegations made by the tenant. According to the land-lord, the tenant was a habitual defaulter and he did not pay rent for Poush and Magh of 1973 B.S. and as such the rent remitted by the tenant for the month of Falgoon was not accepted by him. According to the landlord, the tenant was already a defaulter in payment of monthly rent in terms of the statute; he is, therefore, not entitled to deposit the rent for the months of Polish, Magh and Falgoon, 1373 B.S. 

 4. The learned Rent Controller rejected the application on consideration of the materials on record. According to the learned Rent Controller, the payment of rent for Poush and Magh, 1373 B.S. by the petitioner was not proved. The tenant did not remit rent for Faigoon within the lime provided for in the statute, namely, under Sections 18(5) and 19(1) and accordingly the tenant was not entitled to deposit the rent. 

 5. On appeal the learned District Judge affirmed, the decision of the learned Rent Controller holding that the tenant became a defaulter for non-payment of rent for the months of Poush and Magh and accordingly was not entitled to deposit rent as prayed for. 

 6. Mr. Habib Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the tenant petitioner contends that the learned District judge' exercised jurisdiction not vested in law by holding the petitioner to be a defaulter. According to the learned Advocate, the learned District Judge, while considering the application for deposit of rent under Section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, had no jurisdiction to record a finding that the tenant was a defaulter. Elaborating his contention Mr. Habib Ahmed submits whether the tenant was a defaulter or not, the Rent Controller was required to confine his considerations within the scope of section 17(1) of the said Ordinance. Although there is reference to Section 18, Mr. Habib Ahmed contends that for the purpose of Section 19(1) (a) the finding that the tenant is a defaulter is beyond the jurisdiction of the Rent Controller. 

 7. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the landlord opposite party contends that the expression `a defaulter' used by the learned District Judge Means a person who failed to comply with the requirements of the statute under Section 18. According to him the expression 'a defaulter' means a person who failed to pay rent in terms of the statute. 

 8. In view of the contention raised by the learned Advocate, it is necessary to examine the relevant provisions of Sections 18 and 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. 

 “18 (1). Notwithstanding anything contained in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, or the Contract Act, 1872, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made as long as the tenant pays rent to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance and performs the conditions of the tenancy: 

 "18(5). No tenant shall be entitled to the benefit of this section in respect of any premises unless, he pays the rent due by him in respect of such premises to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance within the time fixed in the contract with his landlord or in the absence of such contract, by the fifteenth day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable, or in the cases provided for in section 19, unless the tenant has deposited such rent or any sub-sequent rent in respect of such premises as provided in that section together with, in the case mentioned in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of that section, the cost of transmission referred to in that clause within the time specified in that section. 

 Explanation—A landlord shall not for the purposes of this sub-section be deemed to have refused to accept any rent unless the rent is remitted within the period referred to above in this sub-section by postal money order to the address of the landlord and the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as undelivered either on account of the landlord having refused to accept payment thereof or for any other clause." 

 "19(1) When a landlord refuses to accept any rent referred to in section 18 remitted by postal money order by a tenant in respect of any premises, the tenant may- 

 (a) deposit such rent within a fortnight of the date on which the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as undelivered, and 

 (b) unless the landlord signifies by notice in writing to the tenant his willingness to accept any subsequent rent which becomes due in respect of such premises, also deposit such subsequent rent within a fort-night of the date on which such rent becomes due, from the expiry of the time within which such rent is required to be paid under sub-section (5) of Section 18 together with the cost of transmission by postal money order of the money deposited to the landlord. 

 9. Reading the above provisions together, it appears that under sub-section (1) of section 18, a protection has been given to the tenant against any order or decree for recovery of possession in respect of any premises so long as the tenant pays rent to the full extent and perform the conditions of the tenancy: In other words, a benefit has been accorded in favour of the tenant to possess the premises as tenant so long he pays rent to the full extent allowable by the Ordinance and carry out the conditions of the tenancy. The benefit assumes the character of a right under the Ordinance but subject to the restrictions contained in the provisos (a) to (b) of section 18(1). Therefore, sub-section (l) of section 18 enables: the tenant to possess the premises as of right on payment of rent to the full extent allowable by the Ordinance subject to the provisos (a) to (e); In Sub-section (5) of section 18, the benefit, given under sub-section (1) of section 18 has been burdened with an 'obligation a the tenant to pay rent in respect of the premises occupied by him to the full extent allowable by the Ordinance within the time fixed in contract between the landlord and the tenant or, in the absence of such contract by the 15th day of the month next following that for which rent is payable. The obligation is to be dis-charged by the tenant in order to enjoy the right and benefit enjoined by the statute against any decree or order for eviction. Further beneficial provisions have been made to Safe-guard the interest of the tenant against refusal of the landlord to accept rent tendered by the tenant within the time provided in the Statute or by the contract. The tenant may deposit the rent. In doing so, the tenant cannot run to the Controller forthwith. He has to remit the rent to the landlord the, time specified in the statute or in, the contract as the case may be. If the landlord accepts the rent remitted, it amounts to payment of rent in accordance with law. In the event the landlord refuses to, accept the rent remitted provisions for making deposit of rent have been made in section 19(1) of the Ordinance. Further provisions have been made for deposit, of rent for any subsequent month in section 19(1) (b). The explanation, to section 18(5) makes the situation clear. It explains that a landlord shall not for the purposes of sub-section(5), of section 18 be deemed to have refused to accept rent unless the sent is remitted within the period referred to above in this sub-section by postal money order to the address of the landlord and the remittance is returned to the tenant ,due to the landlord s refusal to accept payment, or for any other cause. The expression "unless the, rent is remitted within the period, referred to above" is significant and appears to be the essence of Section 18(5). In other words the remittance of rent should be made within the period allowable by this ordinance namely, within the time stipulated in the contract or in the absence of such contract, by the 15th day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable. The remittance should be made to the address of the landlord. If the money order is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities because of the landlord's refusal to accept the remittance of rent or for any other cause, the tenant may make the, deposit accompanied by an application before the Rent Controller. The contents of such application have been specifically stated in section 19(5) of the Ordinance. The deposit under section 19(1) is required to be made under clause (a) within the fortnight of the date on which the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as undelivered. Clause (b) of 19(1) permits the tenant, deposit subsequent rent within a fortnight of the date on which such rent becomes due, together with the cost of transmission by postal money order. 

 10. Thus, in order to enjoy the benefit conferred by section 18(1) of the Ordinance, a tenant is required to, rent within the period of contract or in the absence of such contract by the 15th day of the month next following, that for which the rent is payable. In the event the landlord refuses to accept rent tendered within the time slated above, the tenant is to remit the rent to the address of the landlord within the period referred, to above. If the landlord refuses to accept the rent so remitted, the tenant way deposit such rent within the fortnight of the date on which the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as non-delivered. The deposit shall be accompanied by an application stating the particulars mentioned in Section 19(5). 

 11. With the compliance of the obligations referred to above, the tenant, continues to remain under the protection contained in sub-section (1) of Section 18 and his right to stay in the premises as tenant, remains unaffected. A default in discharging the obligations referred to above takes away the benefit extended to the tenant. The question of default arises with reference to the duty imposed on the tenant by the statute. Section 19(1) refers to section 18. On refusal of the landlord to accept remittance of rent referred to in section 18(5) and the explanation, the tenant acquires the right to deposit rent under Section 19(1) of the Ordinance. Evidently this is a contingent right. Thus, a tenant is, permitted in law to deposit rent under the situation mentioned above. Section 19(5) requires the tenant to state in the application the reasons and circumstances which led the tenant to deposit the rent. The Rent Controller en being satisfied that the tenant has performed what he was required to do under the law may accept the deposit and thereafter shall act in terms of sub-section 6 of section 19 of the Ordinance. Therefore, it follows that a tenant who has failed to satisfy the requirements-noted above is not permitted in law to deposit rent in terms of Section 19(1) of the Ordinance. 

 12. The Controller is not a liaison officer between the landlord and the tenant "Controller" has been defined in section 2(1) of the Ordinance. He is appointed to exercise the powers and discharge, the duties conferred and imposed upon him by or under the ordinance. Therefore the Rent Controller while examining the requirements of section. 19(1) has a duty to look into whether or not the tenant satisfied the requirements of section 18(5) read with the explanation and that he has come within the time mentioned in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 19. In this view of the matter the finding that the tenant is a defaulter is for the purpose of an enquiry under section 19(1). Such finding in a proceeding under section 19(1) of the Ordinance, by itself, does not arm the landlord with a weapon to sue the tenant for ejectment. In a suit for ejectment, it is the landlord who is to prove that the tenant is a defaulter within the meaning of sub-section (5) of section 18. Evidently, there is an inter-relation between sections 18 and 19. In a suit for ejectment, a deposit, not in accordance with section 19(1) is of no assistance to the tenant inasmuch as section 18, for that purpose is not subject to the provisions of, 19(1). Where the requirements of section 19(1) have been lawfully complied with, the deposit made under section 19 will control sub-section (5) of section 18. In such circumstances, a deposit under section 19(1) wilt amount to a payment of rent within the meaning of sub-section (5) of-section 18. In the context of what has been said above, the instant case, the courts below found that the defendant failed to prove payment, of rent for, Poush and Magh, 1373 B.S. within the time contemplated by the statute. The record does not indicate that rent was remitted, by the tenant within the time specified by the statute. Therefore, the Rent Controller was perfectly justified in refusing to accept the deposit of rent since the same was not made within the time and in terms of the statute in the circumstances the contention of Mr. Habib, Ahmed is of no substance.
